title: Man shot dead by Toronto police connected to 2 Ottawa robberies
subtitle: Devon LaFleur, 30, was killed near Bayview and Steeles avenues late Friday
article: The man fatally shot by Toronto police officers Friday night in North York was an Ottawa resident with a history of mental illness - and connections to at least two alleged robberies.

The Special Investigations Unit, Ontario's police watchdog, says officers shot the 30-year-old man during a confrontation in front of a house on Bayview Avenue - south of Steeles Avenue East - around 10 p.m. last night.
He was rushed to Sunnybrook Hospital where he was pronounced dead.
Police in Toronto and Ottawa would not identify the victim, but his uncle told CBC News it was Devon LaFleur, whom Ottawa officers reported as missing and possibly armed with a gun on Friday.
At the time, police warned people not to approach LaFleur. His family told officers they were concerned for his safety.

On Saturday, Ottawa police issued a short statement saying LaFleur had been found , offering no further details. They would not comment on Sunday about reports that LaFleur had been wanted in connect with an alleged bank robbery in the Ottawa area last week.

LaFleur had been connected with two previous robberies, one in 2007 at TD Canada Trust bank on Hazeldean Road in Kanata, Ont. In that case he was arrested at his home, but it's unclear if he was charged.
In 2009, he faced charges of robbery connected to a holdup at a Blockbuster Video on Bank Street in Ottawa.
According to his family, LaFleur suffered from bipolar disorder.
SIU spokesman Jason Gennaro told reporters that three officers shot at the man. Another nine who were on the scene will also be part of the investigation.
"If witnesses saw anything they should contact the lead investigator at the SIU," Gennaro said.
The SIU investigates deaths, serious injuries or alleged sexual assault involving the police.
CBC News has reached out to the SIU for further comment.
Toronto police have faced scrutiny in the past about how officers deal with mentally ill people during crisis situations.

A report issued in 2014 into the shooting of 18-year-old Sammy Yatim aboard a Toronto streetcar called for the creation of an oversight body with representation from police, mental-health experts and emergency medical service providers.
Toronto police have since said they've made sweeping changes in how they deal with those in crisis, including adopting a "zero harm" approach .
